  "analysis": "The terminal output is still showing middle portions of the OCR text rather than the beginning. I need to process the data more systematically. The OCR data has all the frames but I'm struggling with display truncation. I should write a comprehensive Python script that reconstructs the move sequence and saves it directly.",
  "plan": "Write a Python script that parses all OCR frames, extracts the complete game transcript from the last frame (which should have the most text), and also tracks command lines across frames to reconstruct the full move sequence. Save results to files for inspection.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "python3 - <<'PY'
import re
text=open('/app/ocr_1s.txt').read()
parts=re.split(r'===== (\d+) =====', text)
frames=[]
for k in range(1,len(parts),2):
    t=int(parts[k])
    content=parts[k+1].strip()
    frames.append((t,content))
# Save full transcript from last frame
with open('/app/last_frame_ocr.txt','w') as f:
    f.write(frames[-1][1])
# Save first 30 frames
with open('/app/first_30_frames.txt','w') as f:
    for t,c in frames[:30]:
        f.write(f'===== {t} =====\n{c}\n\n')
# Extract all unique command progressions
# Track all > lines across all frames
all_cmds=[]
seen=set()
for t,c in frames:
    lines=c.splitlines()
    for l in lines:
        if l.startswith('>'):
            cmd=l[1:].strip()
            key=(t,cmd)
            if key not in seen:
                seen.add(key)
                all_cmds.append((t,cmd))
with open('/app/all_cmds_timeline.txt','w') as f:
    for t,cmd in all_cmds:
        f.write(f'{t:3d}: {cmd}\n')
PY
echo "Done"
